title: Rolling-window frequency drift versus cumulative frequency and exact uniform 5-of-40 baseline
hypothesis: If the number process is nonstationary, a strictly prior rolling-frequency model may improve the next five-number set probability and marginal inclusion calibration relative to both the exact uniform 5-of-40 model and cumulative-history frequency.

models.M0: Uniform exact 5-of-40 set distribution; each subset has probability 1/C(40,5), each number inclusion probability 5/40.
models.set_probability: P(S|w)=prod_{n in S} w_n / e_5(w), where e_5 is the fifth elementary symmetric polynomial over all 40 weights. This is an exact normalized fixed-size weighted-without-replacement distribution.

protocol.walk_forward: For each target index t, all counts use only rows with index < t. Score before updating counts with the target draw.
protocol.selection: Choose one W on Validation by minimum mean joint set log-loss; ties choose the larger W. Blind OOS is not used for selection.
primary_metrics: marginal inclusion Brier averaged over 40 numbers

inference.method: one-sided paired block sign-flip, contiguous block length 20
inference.holm_family: 12 endpoints: 5 rolling windows vs M0 (two metrics each), plus selected W vs M1 (two metrics).

protocol.secondary: Top20 ranking from marginal inclusion probabilities; report mean hits and 5/5 count descriptively, without promotion.

leakage_checks: window contains at most W prior draws
future-suffix mutation invariance at 9 fixed targets
exact subset probability normalization by exhaustive enumeration for representative forecasts
guardrails: Research only; no production scorer changes.
No Q60 record or existing freeze changes.
Do not reconstruct missing historical freezes.
Historical Blind OOS is not a virgin holdout after prior SONAR research.
next_action: Freeze a Q120-only rolling-frequency Top20 for 2026-11-11 with cutoff 2026-11-10; evaluate only after official publication.
